lines.text: I do, as I say, love these books with all my heart--and I love you too.
lines.note: Robert's early open declaration that he loves her.

lines.text: I thank you, dear Mr. Browning, from the bottom of my heart.
lines.note: Elizabeth's first grateful reply to his letter.

lines.text: Real warm Spring, dear Miss Barrett, and the birds know it; and in Spring I shall see you, surely see you--for when did I once fail to get whatever I had set my heart upon?
lines.note: Robert's spring hope of finally seeing her.

lines.text: And I have the cream of it in your friendship, and a little more, and I do not envy much the milkers of the cows.
lines.note: Elizabeth calls his friendship the cream of her world.

lines.text: And you do like the 'Duchess,' as much as you have got of it? that delights me, too--for every reason.
lines.note: Robert says he loves to see her from week to week.

lines.text: I never shall forget these things, my dearest friend; nor remember them more coldly.
lines.note: Elizabeth promises she will never remember these things coldly.

lines.text: The poems ... yours ... which you left with me,--are full of various power and beauty and character, and you must let me have my own gladness from them in my own way.
lines.note: Elizabeth praises the poems' various power and beauty.

lines.text: I am not conscious of thinking or feeling but about you, with some reference to you--so I will live, so may I die!
lines.note: Robert says his whole life is wound around her.

lines.text: You cannot guess what you are to me--you cannot--it is not possible:--and though I have said that before, I must say it again ... for it comes again to be said.
lines.note: Elizabeth says Robert cannot guess what he is to her.

lines.text: My love--no words could serve here, but there is life before us, and to the end of it the vibration now struck will extend--I will live and die with your beautiful ring, your beloved hair--comforting me, blessing me.
lines.note: Robert vows to live and die with her ring and hair.

lines.text: And therefore, because you are the best, only dearest!——Robert.
lines.note: Elizabeth first speaks the name Robert.

lines.text: Altogether, then, I forgive you, Robert—and it is glorious for me to have something to forgive you for, who are the best so out of measure!—I seize the opportunity.
lines.note: Elizabeth forgives Robert and says she loves him.

lines.text: Ever dearest, your ‘Hush’ came too late.
lines.note: Elizabeth says his 'Hush' came too late after she had spoken.

lines.text: Dearest Ba, the love was as you admit, beneath all the foolish words—I will lay your pardon to my heart with the other blessings.
lines.note: Robert says his love is beneath her goodness.
